The sender mentions receiving a letter from Ruth and expresses hope that the 616 Palm camera can be obtained. --- Page 1 (Beckerman_48a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth: Just got back from my trip yesterday. It was really nice. Went up north of there into Upper Luzon. Scenery is surprisi- ingly pretty - consisting mainly of rice paddies. The rural towns are a pitiful sight dirty old bamboo shacks something at the level of chinese coolies. Each town however has a crude place they call "cabarets" with a covering sign "Welcome Joe". To the philipp ino all americans are called "Joe". On my arrival back I found your wonderful letter from Ruth and then that nice to read of all your homedowns - The new parade block parties and new goods on [illegible] in [illegible] ate I left [illegible] to [illegible] you [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_48b) --- coming home. If you haven't mailed the 616 Palm I wish you'd hold off. My camera's broken and not one around here seems to have a 616. [illegible] 620 or 627 would do much better. Thanks for the favor. I'm so glad you liked the gifts I sent. Picked them up just before leaving Australia. Don't worry Ruth - have something on the way for you. (Please tell me your shoe size.) Mom was letters are getting better all the time. Keep your chin up and we'll be back before you know it. And sincere thanks for your congratulations and many [illegible] thoughts. Still no word from Abe. Love and Regards.
